newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHASTENED MILAN CANNOT AFFORD TO FAIL AGAINST ROSENBORG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHASTENED MILAN CANNOT AFFORD TO FAIL AGAINST ROSENBORG.

text.p: AC Milan will have the worrying prospect of a quarter-final against European Cup holders Juventus on their minds when they travel to Norway to meet Rosenborg in the Champions' League on Wednesday.
"We've got to get a result without being too fussy about how we get it," said striker Marco Simone.
Milan, one of the class acts of European soccer, put themselves under some pressure with a shock 3-2 home defeat by Porto in the first round of the group phase.
If they finish second in group D there is every prospect that they will meet Juventus, the likely group C winners, in the last eight.

Milan, chasing a record-equalling sixth European Cup, appeared to put a mini-crisis behind them with Sunday's 2-1 away win over Bologna in serie A. The victory followed successive defeats by Porto and Sampdoria.
Coach Oscar Washington Tabarez is hopeful that veteran defender Franco Baresi will have recovered from injury to replace the cup-tied Pietro Vierchowod.
If Baresei fails a fitness test then Tabarez can play either Filippo Galli or Marcel Desailly alongside Alessandro Costacurta, with Edgar Davids replacing Desailly in midfield.

Whatever the formation, the Milan defence will have to keep a close watch on the predatory Harald Brattbakk, Rosenborg's leading marksman this season and scorer of one the goals in their impressive 3-2 away win over Gothenburg a fortnight ago.

Juventus, who gave Manchester United a lesson in the finer points of the game in Turin two weeks ago, warmed up for their tie against Fenerbahce in Istanbul with a 2-1 away win over Perugia on Sunday.
Coach Marcello Lippi is expected to make several changes for the trip to Turkey. "The whole point of a large squad is to make changes and to rotate the players," he said.
Central striker Christian Vieri, dropped against Perugia, returns in place of Nicola Amoruso alongside Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero in attack.
Frenchmen Didier Deschamps and Zinedine Zidane are likely to be partnered by Antonio Conte in midfield.
Manchester United, their collective ego bruised by their humbling in Turin, could give expensive, out-of-favour striker Andy Cole his first start of the season in the home match against Rapid Vienna.
Cole made his fourth substitute appearance in the goalless premier league draw against Aston Villa on Saturday.
Rapid's midfield will be significantly weakened at Old Trafford by the absence of Christian Prosenik. He injured his right knee at the weekend.

Ajax Amsterdam, 1-0 away winners over French champions Auxerre in their opening Champions' League fixture, would normally have expected to see off the challenge of Grasshopper Zurich on Wednesday with something to spare.
But these are not normal times for last season's beaten finalists. Wretched league form has left them eight points behind leaders Feyenoord.

Nigerian winger Tijjani Babangida, John Veldman, Richard Witschge, Patrick Kluivert and Peter Hoekstra are all sidelined by injury, while defender Winston Bogarde is an unlikely starter because of a sore foot.
On the bright side, skipper Danny Blind returns from injury.
Atletico Madrid's stunning Champions' League debut, a 4-0 win over former winners Steaua Bucharest, was at odds with some mixed league form.
But a 3-0 win over Logrones on Saturday has put the side in good heart for the trip to Poland to face Widzew Lodz.
Playmaker Jose Luis Caminero will miss Wednesday's game through suspension, while midfielder Juan Vizcaino and forward Leonardo Biagini are doubtful because of injury.

Steaua also have problems ahead of their clash with German champions Borussia Dortmund. They will be without the suspended Adrian Ilie and Marius Baciu and Marius Lacatus and Daniel Prodan, both injured.

Dortmund hardly put themelves in the right frame of mind when they were thrashed 5-1 by Borussia Moenchenglandbach on Saturday. Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said "individual selfishness" had caused the debacle.

Auxerre will be without their two central defenders when they take on Rangers in Glasgow. Captain and sweeper Franck Silvestre is out with a shoulder injury while Australian Ned Zelic has knee problems.
Neither side can afford to lose after suffering defeats in their opening games.
